## What, why and prior learning {#gac3-purpose .gac-lesson }

```{=html}
<div class="gac-intentions">
<div class="gac-intention"><strong>What?</strong><p>We are learning to use the first derivative to identify increasing, decreasing and stationary behaviour and classify stationary points.</p></div>
<div class="gac-intention"><strong>Why?</strong><p>AI training uses the sign of a derivative to decide whether increasing or decreasing a model parameter will reduce prediction error.</p></div>
<div class="gac-intention gac-prior"><strong>Prior learning</strong><p>From Year 11: interpreting derivative signs, finding stationary points and determining increasing and decreasing intervals.</p></div>
</div>
```

::: notes
2 minutes including the cover. Success criterion: I can use a first-derivative sign table to justify where a function increases or decreases and classify its stationary points.

The supplied Year 11 booklet, Section 3.3, pp. 30–36, establishes this prior learning. Its Examples 3.9–3.12 closely match current Examples 1.10–1.12 and 1.14. Last lesson calculated second and higher derivatives; today we use the first derivative geometrically.
:::
